'''Kevin Reitzel''' (Bravo Leader; anagram [[Velken Tezeri]]) finished 4th at the [[1996 Decipher World Championship]] in Vail, Colorado. He later worked for Decipher. The published fan Squadron table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

This page is a '''fan encyclopedia''' stub. It records only published SWCCG-related facts. It is not a biography and does not add private life.

== Tournament results ==
* [[Kevin Reitzel Yavin 4 Occupation Deck]] (DS, August 1999)
* [[Kevin Reitzel Search and Attack Deck]] (LS, July 1999)

* 4th, [[1996 Decipher World Championship]] — [[1996 Decipher World Championship Kevin Reitzel DS|Death Star]] / [[1996 Decipher World Championship Kevin Reitzel LS|Yavin 4: Massassi Throne Room]]
* Las Vegas regional champion, summer 1996 (his account; qualified him for Vail)

== Squadron listing ==

{| class="wikitable"

| Bravo Leader || Decipher Inc. || Retired

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Anagrams ==

A GeoCities fan page (copied onto Encyclopedia 3.2 p.200) maps these printed titles:

* [[Velken Tezeri]] — Kevin Reitzel, Bravo Leader

== Other sourced notes ==

Bravo Leader at Decipher Inc. RFD broadcast 3 (18 December 1998) interviewed him with Kyle Heuer as a new marketing-team member. A fan world-finals history page lists Kevin Reitzel among the 1996 Vail world-final field (Joe Alread 3rd, Reitzel 4th). He published the 1996 pair he kept, 29 years and then 30 years on.

The anagram list unscrambles [[Velken Tezeri]] as Kevin Reitzel.
